references.text: Jabin, king of Hazor, is also mentioned here as an enemy of Israel, showing a continuing conflict with this Canaanite kingdom.
The Lord sold Israel into the hand of their enemies because of their sin, the same pattern repeated in the book of Judges.
God warned that He would sell Israel to their enemies as punishment for disobedience.
The psalmist complains that God has sold His people without gain, a theme reflecting Israel's experience under foreign oppression.
The Lord speaks of having sold Israel because of their sins, the same theological concept.
Sisera is mentioned again in connection with his flight and death, continuing the story of this military commander.
Deborah's song describes the battle against Sisera and the kings of Canaan at Megiddo.
Samuel mentions Sisera as one of the enemies the Lord used to punish Israel when they turned away from Him.
